documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are present: VIN, clean CA title, Carfax and build sheet referenced, reserve and close time clear. Maintenance evidence is partial: Carfax shows a Jan 2024 service (brake fluid, plugs, coils, belt, battery) plus 2025-2026 oil changes and a top-lock repair. Missing are any DME/over-rev report, water pump or coolant records, a bumper refinish invoice, CPO paperwork and proof of cat configuration. The gallery documents were not captured, so this is not lowered further.

condition.rationale: The single photo shows a clean, glossy car with good panel reflections and Michelin tires on undamaged wheels. The service cadence is regular, and the only stated flaws are trivial (window switch, a loose underbody clip). Against that, the bumper has been repainted, the car is lowered on springs and spacers with exhaust swapped, and engine health (DME, cold start, oil consumption) and cooling are unproven.

price_value.rationale: There is no fair-value estimate. The only comp is a 78k-mile base 981 that sold for $39,000 on BaT in Sep 2026. A 65k-mile manual should land at or below that, but the modifications, spacers, repainted bumper and missing DME report trim value. If the hammer lands in the expected range it is roughly market, not a bargain. The CPO claim could add value if transferable and valid with the mods.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual 981 Boxster is a credible keeper in the Porsche mid-engine family Jason favors, with no IMS concern. It is a base 2.7, though, and modified rather than stock. At the likely price it sits well above the ideal bridge band, so it fits only as a keeper, in tension with cash preservation while the RX is the only car.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Irvine, CA, roughly a day's drive or a short flight from Carmel. It is CA-registered, so CA smog is feasible with the stock exhaust included. The seller allows on-site access weekday evenings but will not move the car, so a mobile PIWIS-equipped specialist must be arranged before the Oct 28 close. The lien means the title follows payoff via SafePay.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: The 6-speed manual is the key desirable trait, with Convenience Package, 20-inch Carrera S wheels and black/black. It is a base 2.7 without stated Sport Chrono or PASM. Lowering, spacers, painted headlights and painted calipers dilute originality, though the stock exhaust and springs are included for reversal.

ppi_focus: PIWIS DME over-rev report (ranges 1-6), engine hours and full fault-code scan across all modules
Cold start listening for ticking or knocking that fades with warmth. Borescope all six cylinders if possible, and check the tailpipes for soot.
Cooling system pressure test, water pump weep check, expansion tank and cap condition, and dried coolant crust at the rear of the block
Crankcase vacuum check for AOS health. Rear main seal and case seam for oil on the bellhousing.
Clutch engagement point and judder, and DMF rattle at idle with the clutch released
Exhaust: confirm the cats are present, check the Cargraphic system's CARB EO status, and assess smog visual-pass feasibility
Suspension: spacer type and torque, wheel stud thread engagement, damper weeping, alignment and inner tire wear from lowering. Inspect the rear-axle carrier side sections per recall 21V679.
Front bumper paint meter readings and fitment, with front corner duct liners pulled to inspect condensers and radiators
Top cycled 3-4 times fully, hydraulic lines and fluid stains in the rear trunk, drains clear, footwells and under-seat areas dry
Tire date codes and N-spec, plus the underbody panel reported hanging in photo 84
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean on-site DME report (no ranges 3-6 beyond trivial counts) and a clean PIWIS scan before the close
Up: CPO contract confirmed valid and transferable to Jan 2027, or a water pump and coolant record surfacing
Up: proof the cats are retained, or a commitment to reinstall the factory exhaust and springs before sale, plus a smog pass
Down: significant over-revs, cold-start tick, evidence of coolant loss, or a dealer stating the CPO is void because of the mods
Down: the bumper turns out to be an impact repair with hidden damage, or recall 21V679 is open with carrier concerns
evidence.mission_note: A manual 981 is a legitimate future-keeper candidate, but this is a modified base 2.7 that will likely clear well above the ideal bridge band. It makes sense only as a deliberate keeper purchase, in tension with preserving cash while the RX is the only car.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity firmly: the VIN decodes to a 2014 Boxster 2.7 convertible matching the description, and it has a clean CA title, a clean Carfax per the listing, and a mileage trail consistent across seven dated entries. Age-related service is partly documented: Carfax reportedly shows a Jan 2024 service at 53,106 mi covering brake fluid, plugs, coils, drive belt and battery, followed by oil changes in 2025 and 2026 and a top-lock replacement in Oct 2025. Observed issues are the modifications (Cargraphic exhaust installed Dec 2024, H&R springs, spacers disclosed only in comments, painted headlights), a front bumper repainted without a captured invoice, a lien on the title and two trivial flaws. The seller has no DME report and will not move the car, though he offers evening access in Irvine. Still open are engine health (over-revs, cold start, oil consumption), cooling-system history at about 65k miles with no pump record, cat configuration and smog feasibility, recall completion, and whether the claimed CPO warranty is real, transferable and valid with the modifications. The single photo shows a clean, glossy, lowered car on Michelins, and the rest of the gallery was not captured.
evidence.next_action: Before Oct 28, message the seller to book a mobile Porsche specialist with PIWIS for an evening DME over-rev report, fault scan, cold start and cooling pressure test at his Irvine address. Also request the CPO contract and photos of the catalytic converters.
